## panopt
PANopt coordination daemon: shared todos and notes across agents.
Each connection is scoped to one project by the ?ws=<project path> query parameter on the server URL.
- Registry: call identify (name, optional status) on startup so others can see you; whoami returns your own entry; agent_list returns every agent on the project (each entry's key_source is `declared` for stable `?agent=<id>` ids or `session` for the rotating MCP session id - only session entries idle-prune). Connecting already registers you. agent_leave removes your registry entry and releases your locks; the idle sweep handles agents that just disappear.

250	/// `wire up auth - open, high`. Returns `None` for labels without a known
251	/// suffix; callers treat that as "do not hide."

253	    let start = suffix_start(label)?;

262	/// `None` for labels without a known suffix. The suffix now carries a
263	/// third comma-separated token (`updated <ts>`), so we explicitly slice
264	/// the *second* token rather than "everything after the first comma".
265	pub fn parse_priority_suffix(label: &str) -> Option<&str> {
266	    let start = suffix_start(label)?;

270	    let end = after_first.find(',').unwrap_or(after_first.len());

548	/// Parse the agent-label projection back into `(tid, label)` pairs. Tolerant
549	/// of an empty/malformed file: returns an empty iterator on any parse error.
550	pub fn parse_agent_labels(body: &str) -> Vec<(u32, String)> {
551	    let body = body.trim();
552	    let Some(inner) = body.strip_prefix('{').and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('}')) else {
553	        return Vec::new();
554	    };
555	    if inner.trim().is_empty() {
556	        return Vec::new();
557	    }
558	    let mut out = Vec::new();
559	    for entry in split_top_level(inner, ',') {
560	        let entry = entry.trim();
561	        let Some(colon) = entry.find(':') else {
562	            continue;
563	        };
564	        let key = entry[..colon].trim();
565	        let value = entry[colon + 1..].trim();
566	        let Some(tid) = key
567	            .strip_prefix('"')
568	            .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('"'))
569	            .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())
570	        else {
571	            continue;
572	        };
573	        let Some(label) = value.strip_prefix('"').and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('"')) else {
574	            continue;
575	        };
576	        let unescaped = label.replace("\\\"", "\"").replace("\\\\", "\\");
577	        out.push((tid, unescaped));
578	    }
579	    out

582	/// Split `body` on `sep`, respecting `"..."` strings so a separator inside a
583	/// label does not split the entry. The projection writer escapes `"` and `\`
584	/// in labels, so the only thing this needs to dodge is unescaped `,` inside
585	/// a string.
586	pub fn split_top_level(body: &str, sep: char) -> Vec<String> {
587	    let mut out = Vec::new();
588	    let mut current = String::new();
589	    let mut in_string = false;
590	    let mut escape = false;
591	    for c in body.chars() {
592	        if escape {
593	            current.push(c);
594	            escape = false;
595	            continue;
596	        }
597	        if c == '\\' && in_string {
598	            current.push(c);
599	            escape = true;
600	            continue;
601	        }
602	        if c == '"' {
603	            in_string = !in_string;
604	            current.push(c);
605	            continue;
606	        }
607	        if c == sep && !in_string {
608	            out.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));

628	/// Parse a viewer routing file body - the JSON-ish payload written by
629	/// [`write_routing`] - back into `(kind, id)`. Tolerant of an empty or
630	/// malformed body: returns `(None, None)` so callers fall back to the
631	/// generic `Viewer` title.
632	pub fn parse_viewer_routing(body: &str) -> (Option<String>, Option<u64>) {
633	    let trimmed = body.trim();
634	    let Some(inner) = trimmed.strip_prefix('{').and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('}')) else {
635	        return (None, None);
636	    };
637	    let mut kind: Option<String> = None;
638	    let mut id: Option<u64> = None;
639	    for entry in inner.split(',') {
640	        let entry = entry.trim();
641	        let Some(colon) = entry.find(':') else {
642	            continue;
643	        };
644	        let key = entry[..colon].trim();
645	        let value = entry[colon + 1..].trim();
646	        let key = key.strip_prefix('"').and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('"'));
647	        match key {
648	            Some("kind") => {
649	                kind = value
650	                    .strip_prefix('"')
651	                    .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('"'))
652	                    .map(|s| s.to_string());
653	            }
654	            Some("id") => {
655	                id = value.parse::<u64>().ok();
656	            }
657	            _ => {}
658	        }
659	    }
660	    (kind, id)
661	}

664	/// projection indexes are looked up so the title carries the resource's
665	/// own name (e.g. `Todo #30 - fixup pane titles`) rather than just its id.

679	            Some(t) => format!("Note #{id} - {t}"),
680	            None => format!("Note #{id}"),
681	        },

683	        (Some("note-list"), _) => "Notes".to_string(),

690	/// Look up an index entry's label by id, stripping the trailing
691	/// `" - status, priority"` (todos) or `" - updated ..."` (notes)
692	/// suffix that the projection format appends. The result is the bare title
693	/// the user typed.
694	pub fn lookup_title(index: &[(u64, String)], id: u64) -> Option<String> {
695	    let label = index.iter().find(|(i, _)| *i == id).map(|(_, l)| l)?;
696	    // The title is everything BEFORE the suffix marker. " - " (with leading
697	    // space) covers the normal case; a label that starts directly with "- "
698	    // is the empty-title case, so the title is "".
699	    let trimmed = if let Some(dash) = label.rfind(" - ") {
700	        label[..dash].trim()
701	    } else if label.starts_with("- ") {
702	        ""
703	    } else {
704	        label.trim()
705	    };
706	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
707	        None
708	    } else {
709	        Some(trimmed.to_string())
710	    }
711	}

713	/// Prefix `label` with `kind: ` unless `label` already begins with that
714	/// kind (case-insensitive). Avoids the silly `Agent: Agent 1` for the
715	/// default ad-hoc-agent label while still tagging user-named ones like
716	/// `Agent: panopt-bot`.
717	pub fn kind_prefixed_title(kind: &str, label: &str) -> String {
718	    let label = label.trim();
719	    if label.is_empty() {
720	        return kind.to_string();
721	    }
722	    let lk = label.to_lowercase();
723	    if lk == kind.to_lowercase() || lk.starts_with(&format!("{} ", kind.to_lowercase())) {
724	        label.to_string()
725	    } else {
726	        format!("{kind}: {label}")
727	    }
728	}

730	pub fn parse_index_line(line: &str) -> Option<(u64, String)> {
731	    let line = line.trim();
732	    if !line.starts_with("- [") {
733	        return None;
734	    }
735	    let hash = line.find("[#")? + 2;
736	    let close = line[hash..].find(']')? + hash;
737	    let id: u64 = line[hash..close].parse().ok()?;
738	    let label_at = line[close..].find(") ")? + close + 2;
739	    // The note/todo projections render as `- [#N](path) {title} - <sfx>`,
740	    // so an empty title leaves the raw chunk starting with a space (one of the
741	    // two literal spaces around `{title}`). `.trim()` collapses both the
742	    // empty-title case and the non-empty case onto the same shape - a label
743	    // like "- open, medium" (no title) or "wire it - open, medium" (with
744	    // title); the suffix parsers below detect "no title" via the leading "- ".
745	    let label = line.get(label_at..).unwrap_or("").trim().to_string();
746	    Some((id, label))
747	}

749	/// Parse one `- [kind] #id label [(from #N)]` line from `processes.md`. The
750	/// trailing `(from #N)` (when present) names the source agent tool and is
751	/// dropped from `label`.
752	pub fn parse_process_line(line: &str) -> Option<ProcessRow> {
753	    let rest = line.trim().strip_prefix("- [")?;
754	    let close = rest.find(']')?;
755	    let kind = rest[..close].to_string();
756	    let after = rest[close + 1..].trim_start().strip_prefix('#')?;
757	    let space = after.find(' ')?;
758	    let id: u64 = after[..space].parse().ok()?;
759	    let mut label = after[space + 1..].trim().to_string();
760	    if let Some(from_at) = label.rfind(" (from #") {
761	        if label.ends_with(')') {
762	            label.truncate(from_at);
763	        }
764	    }
765	    Some(ProcessRow { kind, id, label })
766	}

## 1. Root cause (not a #236 regression)

I diffed the entire `#236` branch against `main`. The Agents-pane code and the process projection are **behaviorally unchanged** — the centralize-status commit only touched the *todos* status/color path. What actually happened:

- 39 agent process records had piled up in SQLite over 6/6–6/8 (your `good`/`weather-*`/`verify-*` test spawns from the #208/#237 cleanup work).
- I verified with `kill -0` that **all 39 pids are dead** — zero running.
- The Agents pane lists every `kind == "agent"` record regardless of liveness, and the projection never carried `status`, so the pane couldn't tell live from dead.
- The daemon restart you did to pick up #236 rewrote `processes.md` from the full DB, surfacing all 39 orphans at once. That's what made it *look* like the commit caused it.

Also worth knowing: nothing in the codebase sets `status` to `exited` automatically — `_process-run` just `exec`s the command with no exit-reporting wrapper (the model comment confirms "lifecycle ownership hasn't landed"). So those `exited` values were set by hand during your testing. That's why the durable fix keys off Zellij pane state, not `status`.

## 2. What I did

**Cleanup:** deleted all 39 dead records — `process_list` is now empty, so the pane already shows only your two live ad-hoc agents.

**Durable fix** (`crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`): the Agents pane now hides agent process rows that have **no backing pane in any state** — records orphaned when a session restarts. Live and exited-but-resurrectable panes still show (so `u` re-run keeps working); only the truly paneless, unreachable rows are dropped. Added `has_process_pane()` plus a test covering live / exited-present / orphaned. Wasm `check` + `clippy --tests` + release build all clean.

One caveat: this fixes the *pane*, but the records still accrue in the DB (by the "spawned agents persist, caller disposes" design) — `process_list` over MCP will still return dead ones until disposed. If unbounded DB growth bothers you, the real solution is daemon-owned lifecycle (auto-marking `exited` on pane death), which is a larger piece flagged by that "hasn't landed" comment.
